meta.one_liner: Buy quality stocks when they close below the lower Bollinger Band, sell when they snap back to the middle.
meta.explainer_md: Bollinger Bands wrap a 20-day average in a two-standard-deviation envelope — a statistical definition of 'stretched'. A close below the lower band means the stock has fallen unusually far, unusually fast. This strategy buys those closes, but only in stocks still above their 200-day average (healthy uptrends, not collapses), and sells when price recovers to the 20-day middle band. It's the classic rubber-band trade: stretched prices tend to snap back — until the one time they don't, which is why the time-stop matters.

spec.name: Bollinger Band Reversion
spec.description: Close below sma_20 - 2*stddev_20 while above sma_200; exit at the middle band.
